The 1850 United States Census for Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania records five people sharing the surname Flynn living together in dwelling 214. A FamilySearch index of an 1817 Norwegian parish register records the baptism of a boy named Christian Frederich on 20 July 1817 in Stavanger, Rogaland, Norway, nine days after his birth there on 11 July 1817. His father is named Tollev Nadnesen — though that surname is very likely a mis-reading of "Aadnesen," since the Norwegian double-A that begins many patronymics in this region looks like an "N" in old handwriting, and the indexer appears to have made that exact error. His mother is named Inger Larsdatter, meaning daughter of Lars, and she is recorded as residing in Stavanger. The father's residence is given as Birkeland, a farm name in Rogaland that aligns with the child's later known surname, and the father's given name Tollev matches the child's later patronymic Tollefsen (son of Tollef/Tollev).

The most important next step is to view the original parish register image (FamilySearch image group 013729012, approximately images 200–220 covering July 1817) to confirm whether the father's surname is truly Aadnesen or Nadnesen, and to capture any additional detail — such as godparents or witnesses — that the index did not transcribe.
